notes.note: This could be just a B-flat minor. But the way the a flat takes up room at the end of the melody means I'm going with B flat minor seven. But I don't truly know what the rule is it's only played one time it's not playing or played by any accompanying instrument. So maybe it's not part of the chord. Update: the first four notes of the melody (Bb, Db, F, Ab) clearly outline the B flat minor seven chord, and I give that weight.

My confidence level on this chord is very low. Most certainly there is a court change here. the b Stays in the root and that's intentional. The middle voice is doing a G a lot and then going up to a flat

The arpeggio underneath clearly spells out G flat minor, without any doubt. The melody's long E flat is not part of the chord. It is the fifth of the previous chord, held over, and it steps down to the D flat, which is in the chord. That tension and release is a suspension, and my ear confirms the D flat feels like a release.
